posts.raw_content:
Caveat first, because I know many of the people whose names I've forgotten don't even participate on the forum anymore, and so many of you newbies are some serious faggots of various stripes. If you don't know who you are, then you're both a retard and faggot. I'm writing this more for those who are legit, whether or not we actually conversed in a positive way (agreeing or not). Next, because I'm a selfish fuck, and u/SaltyCracker at least has a profile, and I'm a fan if only because he is like a combination of 3 of my high school drinking buddies, and is damn near the same age. 

In case you didn't notice, this one is a TL;DR. I first met my wife somewhere around 18 years ago, it was some random facebook chatroom (we dispute the topics of search that led to us exchanging introductions), for you kids, random chats sometimes crossed paths with someone within a reasonable distance. After some conversations, we decided that meeting wouldn't be a waste of time, I called it a date and she didn't dispute, something simple, IIRC it was coffee and the bowling alley at the local mall, afterwards, I made sure that she was close enough to home that she felt safe.... THEN, she rejects the kiss. 

Instantly written off, if a girl isn't willing to entertain a kiss after the first date, well, sorry, but she's just not that into you. A few days go by and the phone rings, it's her, I answer. She is pissed off at me, "What the fuck, I thought you were having a good time, I was having a good time. Why didn't you call me back?" I was flustered, not only had SHE called me back, she was angry at me that I had given up. I explained my position, and she expected that I would plan another date. 

Years pass, I meet her family, join in their reunions together, they are all deeply connected, and deeply religious. I was never offended by religion, but I had long been agnostic in the sense that I knew there was an afterlife, I viewed it as effectively a requirement of physics as we understand them, even if it's never even alluded to in any text books. In fact, I was raised Catholic, so, I at least knew how to behave even though across the larger family are mostly protestant with some Mennonites. (You don't know how many times I've had to bite my tongue to stop myself from making a joke about Mennonitis, but really, once you get to know them, it's almost one of those that if they hate you it's because YOU fucked up)

 In parts because; her family is primarily engineers and other highly technical fields, she thought that I was more than suited to a career requiring a higher education, her willingness to contribute on top of what I had banked in a career in construction to ensure that I would be able to complete with no extra debt (I had about 2 months after graduating to find a job or I was going back to trades work), and finally, because it really pissed me off how many people would address legitimate criticism of the 9-11 official story as not mattering because "you're not an engineer". 

I knew this woman was faithful to a fault, I had even joked to her at points that even if she DID hit a point of weakness and cheated that, she had so much conscience that she would call me asap crying to tell me that she had fucked up. She had beyond proven her commitment to both me and US as a couple. She had a strong family (especially that I was in a "new" city, even though at that point I was living there 10+ years. But, my family is in Winnipeg and surrounding) It wasn't like I was looking elsewhere, and willing to risk what we had built... I caved to her increasing pressure, bought her a ring and proposed to her in the Calgary Tower. I went all out, I was about to bend the knee and she started smacking me to not make a scene and YES!!!!  

I bet it was not a common issue for the admin, but we thought that classes would start a few weeks later, but we wound up married and on a honeymoon where I had to bring near the weight limit of books to ensure that I didn't return that far behind. Like I said, she was supportive and recognized that she was putting up with an investment. 

Approaching more recently; my wife was working a position where the manager was particularly toxic. Literally, picked her up from work one day and this woman was 175% Karen, ridiculous colored leather jacket, THE Karen haircut, and even the walk spelled entitled bitch. As my wife gets in the car, I point in a way that the woman wouldn't be able to see and ask if that's her. She tells me yes and asks how I knew. It was obvious. So, I tell her that I'm at a point where I'm making enough money that work can be optional for her, she can take whatever time she needs to get back to work, or just to help at home, whatever. This was more or less in the heat of covid, before the mandatory vaccines, but after masking requirements (at least in Canada).  

I haven't mentioned yet, and it wasn't something that I even noticed (in part because she tries to conceal) for probably a month or two into dating, that she had a relatively light expression of cerebral palsy. Her left side was partially paralyzed. I would literally have deserved the scorn from her family if I had rejected her for something she was born with AFTER not noticing for a significant time. She never wanted that to be part of how people viewed her though, she didn't even want to take advantage of benefits that would be offered to her because she wanted to be viewed as "normal". This woman literally ran a bit shy of a 15k because she wanted to hang out with me from her parents house, she lived with them until we were married.

We are approaching the present; about a year to 2 ago I noticed in some lighting that she was showing signs of jaundice and that it should be looked into because even if not necessarily significant, there's enough chance that this is a sign of something serious. She found some home remedies, and since I'm all for avoiding medical intervention if it isn't necessary, and over the following months everything had cleared up and how am I going to argue with what works. 

Give or take a week of a month ago, the jaundice reappears. I tell her that she should set an appointment with her family doctor. She refuses. She's not eating as much and she's starting to vomit a good portion of what she is eating; she tells me she ate too fast, or coughed too hard, or similar. So, I point out other signs, and she tells me that it's probably something else relatively minor. 

Now, she's not really eating food, her diet is reduced to juices, and even then she's sometimes vomiting. I argue harder, "Do you prefer a doctors appointment or me to take you to the hospital?" She would say that she didn't want the prescriptions. I argue back that I don't care if she wants a "home remedy" (because there is a usefulness there) but she needs to at least get a diagnosis to be sure that she's using the right remedies. Eventually, I frame things as something of an ultimatum; "We are going to the hospital if nothing changes tomorrow." She accepts, while asking if I would mind if she slept on the couch that night. 

My plan was to go to work, tell my boss that I had finally convinced my wife to go to hospital and that I would leave early. I'm told that he would ensure that everything was handled and to take the time needed. I get home that evening, my wife is on the couch, she's breathing but clearly in pain. I tell her I'm walking her to the car to go to hospital, she agrees, 5-6 steps later she asks to return to the couch. "If I bring you back to the couch I'm calling an ambulance." I lie her down on the couch. 

After a call to the ambulance where I have to assure them that there are no weapons, no domestic abuse, and that our dog must be kept out of the scene, and about 10-15 minutes wait they show up. It wasn't a minute after they walk in that they look at my wife and, I don't think they actually said it, but I feel like they looked at her and at least thought "oh shit". For the next half hour or so they are taking readings, the dog is barking trying to participate / help / receive attention. In my wife's style, each probe they attach she removes and apologizes, they put a wrap around her head for temperature and she tells them that she doesn't want a hat. As they leave the last EMT in the line turns to tell me that her condition is among the most serious that she had seen and that I need to brace myself for the worst. I contemplate following, but decide that the dog still needs food and a walk and that there's little I can contribute in the first hour(s), so, I start calling her family. 

Day 0 - I'm not even back from walking the dog, family is already starting to show up at the hospital and the doctor is asking if blood transfusions are OK. I say, "She would want to avoid accepting covid vaccinated blood, BUT I want her to live, so, do what needs to be done and let her be mad at me later."

Day 1 - The situation is serious, and we are looking at organ donation, but she needs to show improvement by the time the relevant experts arrive. 

Day 2 - Things remain tenuous, she has 10+ bags of intravenous compounds flowing into her to "throw the book at her". 

Day 3 - It's determined by the people looking at donation candidates that, even with a candidate (they never tell us if such a candidate exists) that given how things have changed that she would be unlikely to survive a surgery to replace the organs. 

At 10PM or so, with her sister, aunts, uncles, cousins and all, it was decided that it was time to turn off life support. That her heart had stopped so quickly is a demonstration of how much the machines were doing the work to keep her alive. 

Thank you for reading our story, at most I will repost with an image of my lost wife. The prayers aren't for me, the prayers I ask for is to reinforce her claim to a spot in heaven. I probably don't deserve it, but, in spite of any flaws she might have had, she does deserve a spot and if the prayers might make any difference, it would be appreciated. 

I'll try to answer questions that come up, but don't be too shitty because I feel shitty enough, like I failed her, without your help.
